etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English ymagynen, from Middle French imaginer, from Latin imāginor, from imāginem, the accusative singular of imāgō (“a copy, likeness, image”).

definitions.definition: (transitive) To form a mental image of something; to envision or create something in one's mind.

quote.citation: 1971, John Lennon (lyrics and music), “Imagine”, in Imagine (album):
quote.text: Imagine all the people / Livin' life in peace

quote.citation: c. 1595–1596 (date written), William Shakespeare, “A Midsommer Nights Dreame”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies: Published According to the True Originall Copies (First Folio), London:  […]  Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act V, scene i], page 159, column 2:
quote.text: Or in the night, imagining ſome feare, / How eaſie is a buſh ſuppos’d a Beare?

quote.citation: 2013 June 14, Jonathan Freedland, “Obama's once hip brand is now tainted”, in The Guardian Weekly, volume 189, number 1, page 18:
quote.text: Now we are liberal with our innermost secrets, spraying them into the public ether with a generosity our forebears could not have imagined. Where we once sent love letters in a sealed envelope, or stuck photographs of our children in a family album, now such private material is despatched to servers and clouds operated by people we don't know and will never meet.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To believe in something created by one's own mind, often something false.
(transitive, obsolete) To contrive in purpose; to scheme; to devise.

quote.citation: 1611, The Holy Bible, […] (King James Version), London:  […]  Robert Barker, […], →OCLC, Psalms 62:3, column 1:
quote.text: How long wil ye imagine miſchiefe againſt a man?

definitions.definition: (transitive, Internet slang, rhetorical, sarcastic) Used to mock an idea by suggesting that it is ridiculous or ill thought through.
(fandom slang) A short fanfic or prompt placing a reader insert in a novel scenario with a character or celebrity.

quote.citation: 2015 March 2, Laura Starling, “FFIC101: An Introduction to the Horrors of Fanfiction”, in Critic, University of Otago, page 21:
quote.text: Some imagines are more sexual and creepy than others: "Imagine Stiles walking in on you giving Scott a blowjob."

quote.citation: 2016 December, Jocelyn Chambers, “The Exclusion Of People Of Color In Fanfiction”, in Majesty, page 96:
quote.text: i personally like imagines and fanfics so i found a good amount of kylo ren x reader fics and started going through them.

quote.citation: 2019, "thranduilsperkybutt", quoted in "Author Spotlight: thranduilsperkybutt", Lemon, February 2019, page 37:
quote.text: If I get inspired immediately, I can bust out an imagine in 5-10 minutes.
